questions.text: In Excel, which formula returns 0 instead of an error when A2 is divided by B2 and B2 happens to be zero or blank?
questions.explanation: IFERROR evaluates the expression and returns the alternative value if it results in an error.
steps: Spot what the question tests: IF, IFERROR, ISERROR.
Option A (=IF(A2/B2,0)) is out: The IF function would itself return the error.
Option B (=ISERROR(A2/B2)) is out: It returns TRUE or FALSE, not a value.
Option C (=A2/B2+0) is out: The error is still returned.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing IF without a test.
So the answer is option D: =IFERROR(A2/B2,0).
wrongReasons: The IF function would itself return the error
It returns TRUE or FALSE, not a value

questions.text: If cell A1 contains 'SSC-CGL-2026', which formula returns 'CGL'?
questions.explanation: MID(text, start, length) starts at character 5, which is the 'C' of CGL.
steps: Spot what the question tests: LEFT, MID, RIGHT.
Option A (=LEFT(A1,3)) is out: Returns SSC.
Option B (=RIGHT(A1,3)) is out: Returns 026.
Option D (=MID(A1,4,3)) is out: Returns -CG.
Common slip to avoid: Starting one character early.
So the answer is option C: =MID(A1,5,3).

questions.text: A formula =$B2*C$1 is entered in cell D2 and copied to cell E3. What formula appears in E3?
questions.explanation: $B stays in column B but the row moves down one, and C$1 moves one column to the right while row 1 is locked.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Mixed references.
Option A (=$B2*D$1) is out: The row of the first reference should move down.
Option B (=$C3*D$1) is out: The column of the first reference is locked.
Option C (=$B3*D$2) is out: The row of the second reference is locked.
Common slip to avoid: Moving a locked part of a reference.
So the answer is option D: =$B3*D$1.
questions.trap: Moving a locked part of a reference.
wrongReasons: The row of the first reference should move down
The column of the first reference is locked
The row of the second reference is locked

questions.text: Which Word feature records every insertion and deletion made by reviewers so that the author can accept or reject them?
questions.explanation: Track Changes marks edits for review.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Review tab features.
Option B (Mail Merge) is out: It merges data into letters.
Option C (Spelling and Grammar) is out: It checks language only.
Option D (Compare Documents) is out: It compares two files after the event.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing Compare.
So the answer is option A: Track Changes.
wrongReasons: It compares two files after the event

questions.text: Which PowerPoint view lets the speaker see notes and the next slide while the audience sees only the current slide?
questions.explanation: Presenter View displays notes and the next slide on the speaker's screen.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Slide show views.
Option B (Slide Sorter) is out: It arranges slides.
Option C (Outline View) is out: It shows text only.
Option D (Normal View) is out: It is for editing.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing Notes Page.
So the answer is option A: Presenter View.

questions.text: Which of the following is provided by a digital signature on a document?
options: Authentication of the sender and integrity of the content
questions.explanation: A digital signature uses the sender's private key to prove origin and detect tampering.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Digital signatures.
Option A (Confidentiality of the content) is out: Encryption provides this, not the signature itself.
Options B and D are out: Not a function.
Common slip to avoid: Believing that signing also encrypts.
So the answer is option C: Authentication of the sender and integrity of the content.
wrongReasons: Encryption provides this, not the signature itself

questions.text: A firewall mainly serves to:
options: filter incoming and outgoing network traffic according to rules
remove all viruses from a computer
questions.explanation: A firewall permits or blocks traffic according to defined rules.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Firewall vs antivirus.
Options A and C are out: Not its function.
Option D (remove all viruses from a computer) is out: That is the job of antivirus software.
Common slip to avoid: Treating a firewall as antivirus.
So the answer is option B: filter incoming and outgoing network traffic according to rules.
wrongReasons: That is the job of antivirus software

questions.text: What is the main purpose of a Virtual Private Network (VPN)?
options: To increase the storage capacity of a server
To create an encrypted tunnel over a public network
questions.explanation: A VPN encrypts traffic between the user and the VPN endpoint.
steps: Spot what the question tests: VPN.
Options A and D are out: Not its function.
Option B (To block advertisements) is out: Not its main function.
Common slip to avoid: Thinking it speeds up the connection.
So the answer is option C: To create an encrypted tunnel over a public network.
questions.trap: Thinking it speeds up the connection.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of a RISC processor compared with a CISC processor?
options: A large set of complex instructions
A small set of simple instructions, mostly of fixed length
Heavy use of microcode for every instruction
Instructions that take variable numbers of bytes
questions.explanation: RISC designs use simple, fixed-length instructions that can be pipelined easily.
steps: Spot what the question tests: RISC vs CISC.
Option A (A large set of complex instructions) is out: This describes CISC.
Options C and D are out: More typical of CISC.
Common slip to avoid: Reversing RISC and CISC.
So the answer is option B: A small set of simple instructions, mostly of fixed length.

questions.text: What happens when a device raises an interrupt while the CPU is executing a program?
options: The CPU saves its state, runs the interrupt service routine and then resumes
The program is deleted from memory
The device takes over the operating system
questions.explanation: The CPU services the interrupt and then returns to the interrupted program.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Interrupt handling.
Options B, C and D are out: Not what happens.
Common slip to avoid: Thinking an interrupt is an error.
So the answer is option A: The CPU saves its state, runs the interrupt service routine and then….
questions.trap: Thinking an interrupt is an error.

questions.text: What is the hexadecimal equivalent of the decimal number 255?
steps: Spot what the question tests: Decimal to hexadecimal.
Option A (EE) is out: Equals 238.
Option B (F0) is out: Equals 240.
Option D (1F) is out: Equals 31.
Common slip to avoid: Writing a wrong digit.
So the answer is option C: FF.

questions.text: At which layer of the OSI model does a router mainly operate?
questions.explanation: Routers forward packets by IP address at layer 3.
steps: Spot what the question tests: OSI layers and devices.
Option A (Data link layer) is out: Used by switches.
Option B (Physical layer) is out: Used by hubs and repeaters.
Option C (Transport layer) is out: Used by TCP and UDP.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing the data link layer.
So the answer is option D: Network layer.

questions.text: Which sequence of segments forms the TCP three-way handshake?
questions.explanation: The client sends SYN, the server replies SYN-ACK, and the client confirms with ACK.
steps: Spot what the question tests: TCP handshake.
Option A (SYN, ACK, FIN) is out: FIN closes a connection.
Option B (ACK, SYN, SYN-ACK) is out: The order is wrong.
Option D (SYN, FIN, ACK) is out: FIN is not part of the opening.
Common slip to avoid: Mixing the order.
So the answer is option C: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK.
wrongReasons: FIN is not part of the opening

questions.text: Which protocol automatically assigns IP addresses to devices on a network?
questions.explanation: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol leases addresses to hosts.
steps: Spot what the question tests: DHCP.
Option A (DNS) is out: Resolves names.
Option B (SMTP) is out: Sends email.
Option C (FTP) is out: Transfers files.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing DNS.
So the answer is option D: DHCP.

questions.text: A table is in second normal form (2NF) if it is in first normal form and:
options: every non-key attribute depends on the whole primary key
questions.explanation: 2NF removes partial dependencies on part of a composite key.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Normal forms.
Option A (it has no transitive dependencies) is out: This is the condition for 3NF.
Option C (every attribute is multi-valued) is out: This violates 1NF.
Option D (it has no primary key) is out: A key is required.
Common slip to avoid: Mixing up 2NF and 3NF.
So the answer is option B: every non-key attribute depends on the whole primary key.

questions.text: In SQL, which clause is used to filter groups after the GROUP BY clause has been applied?
questions.explanation: HAVING applies conditions to aggregated groups.
steps: Spot what the question tests: WHERE vs HAVING.
Option B (WHERE) is out: It filters rows before grouping.
Option C (ORDER BY) is out: It sorts the result.
Option D (DISTINCT) is out: It removes duplicates.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing WHERE.
So the answer is option A: HAVING.

questions.text: A candidate key that is chosen to identify the rows of a table uniquely is called the:
questions.explanation: One candidate key is selected as the primary key.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Types of keys.
Option A (Foreign key) is out: Refers to another table.
Option B (Composite key) is out: Made of more than one column, but not necessarily chosen.
Option C (Secondary key) is out: Not used for unique identification.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing foreign key.
So the answer is option D: Primary key.
wrongReasons: Made of more than one column, but not necessarily chosen

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the three Vs commonly used to describe big data?
questions.explanation: The three Vs are volume, velocity and variety.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Characteristics of big data.
Options A, C and D are out: One of the three Vs.
Common slip to avoid: Not noticing the NOT.
So the answer is option B: Validity.

questions.text: Which feature makes a blockchain record difficult to alter after it has been added?
options: Each block is stored on one central server
Each block contains the hash of the previous block
Blocks are encrypted with a single shared password
questions.explanation: Changing one block changes its hash and breaks all later links.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Blockchain basics.
Option A (Each block is stored on one central server) is out: Blockchains are distributed.
Option C (Blocks are encrypted with a single shared passw…) is out: This is not how immutability arises.
Option D (Blocks are deleted after verification) is out: Records are kept.
Common slip to avoid: Thinking a central authority protects the data.
So the answer is option B: Each block contains the hash of the previous block.
questions.trap: Thinking a central authority protects the data.
wrongReasons: This is not how immutability arises

questions.text: Which of the following is a non-volatile storage device that uses flash memory and has no moving parts?
questions.explanation: An SSD stores data in flash memory without moving parts.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Storage technologies.
Option B (Hard Disk Drive) is out: Uses spinning platters.
Option C (RAM module) is out: Volatile memory.
Option D (Optical disc) is out: Uses a laser and a spinning disc.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing HDD.
So the answer is option A: Solid State Drive.
wrongReasons: Uses a laser and a spinning disc
